{"documentId": "f_1e468a9d69ea0f0a2001f5", "title": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)", "name": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)", "revisionId": "89aa42aa1b", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T23:46:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-12T23:46:00Z", "text": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)
This is the lifestyle route I posted about in #executives. The LLC is the new one Blake and I are setting up for the three of us, and anything Harmony Games owns (the games with their art and listings, and the equipment) comes to it only through Sunset's sale, the way I wrote after the call on Wednesday. Services we keep running just move their billing to the LLC.
The plan runs March 1 to May 31.
Domino Delights and Zombie Match come over only if what each made in January, going by the warehouse's daily revenue table, covers what its own hosting bills now, whatever we said about them before. Combo Fighter comes over either way, it's the reason we're doing this. A game that comes over brings what it needs to keep running, its accounts and its player support.
Cost every item at what it bills now, going by whoever runs it, not by what HG used to pay.
What we already decided to keep or cancel for the shutdown in #winddown stays decided.
Pay for anyone who stays on is a separate conversation once we know the running cost; this plan is only what bills us every month, no one-offs or yearly fees.
How things move is on the LLC card on our board.
"}

content.content: how we split it: each of the three of us carries a third of what the LLC costs a month, March through May. that's everything on the plan that bills monthly, including what one of us already pays for it. whatever one of us already pays personally counts toward his third, and he puts the difference in as cash. put the three shares on the sheet per month.

I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. Hi everyone,
I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.
If you would like to talk 1:1 this week, reply here and I will make time.
Thank you,

{"ts": "1768415499.678309", "type": "message", "text": "What the seed docs imply for your “$2M pre + Griffin matches angels” plan
*1) A $2M pre priced round is a down round vs Seed, and it triggers anti-dilution.*
Series Seed was sold at *$0.9830/share*.
Your Restated Certificate has *broad-based weighted average anti-dilution*: if you issue stock (or “deemed issued” via convertibles) below the current Conversion Price, the Series Seed Conversion Price ratchets down using *CP2 = CP1 * (A + B) ÷ (A + C)*.
Practical effect: a $2M pre priced round will *increase the as-converted share count of Seed*, which *dilutes founders/common more than the headline pre-money suggests*.
*2) You cannot just “issue new shares / a new series” without Preferred consent.*
The Restated Certificate requires Preferred approval (voting as a class on an as-converted basis) for major actions, including:
changing Seed rights
increasing/decreasing authorized Preferred or any additional class/series
• creating a new class/series *unless it is junior* to Preferred
• M&A / liquidation
• dividends/redemptions, subsidiary structure, and even changing board size
*3) Griffin already has an explicit right to buy into the “next Preferred round” up to 33% FD.*
Separate Pro Rata Rights Letter: in the *next bona fide sale of a newly authorized series of Preferred*, Griffin can buy enough to end at *33% fully diluted post-close*, at the same price and terms as other investors.
So “we’ll match angels with $250k” is either:
• a voluntary cap [PERSON_NAME_2000] is imposing on itself for this round, or
• a statement that assumes angels are small enough that $250k gets them where they want, or
• something that needs a side letter clarifying how it interacts with their 33% right.
How to structure “[PERSON_NAME_2000] matches angels with $250k at $2M pre” cleanly
Option A (cleanest): One priced round, one price, one security
• *Single financing* at *$2M pre* with *one set of terms* for angels and [PERSON_NAME_2000].
• [PERSON_NAME_2000] subscribes for *up to $250k* on the same terms.
• Add a *short side letter*: [PERSON_NAME_2000]’s $250k cap is intentional, and [PERSON_NAME_2000] either:
*waives* its ability to buy above $250k for this financing (even if the Pro Rata Letter would allow it), or
keeps the right to go above $250k only if needed to reach a specific agreed ownership threshold (spell it out).
Why this matters: if you do two prices or two different securities, you worsen anti-dilution math and increase “unfairness” perceptions immediately.
Option B: Same priced round, two closings
• Close angels first, then close [PERSON_NAME_2000] shortly after, but *same terms, same price, same security*, documented as one “Financing.”
This still preserves [PERSON_NAME_2000]’s Pro Rata framing and keeps the cap table coherent.
Option C (works if [PERSON_NAME_2000] insists on “better than angels” economics): Same security, structured economics (not two valuations)
If [PERSON_NAME_2000] truly wants “lower valuation than angels,” the least messy way is not two prices. Do one price, and give [PERSON_NAME_2000] a negotiated economic lever that is transparent:
• e.g., same Series seed-extension preferred, but [PERSON_NAME_2000] gets a narrow, defined sweetener (board observer, information covenant, small warrant coverage, etc.).
This still likely needs Preferred consents, but it avoids triggering extra anti-dilution complexity from two separate effective prices.
What to avoid: SAFE at a much lower cap as a workaround. Your charter’s adjustment provisions explicitly contemplate Options/Convertible Securities and can defer adjustments until the economics are calculable, but it does not mean “no anti-dilution impact.”

Your direct question: “How do co-founders maintain their shares without investing cash?”
They can’t maintain *percentage ownership* in an equity financing without someone else taking the dilution. There are only three real levers:
1. *Accept dilution* (they keep their absolute share count, but ownership percent drops).
2. *Get a “founder refresh”* (new option grants or restricted stock grants). This dilutes everyone else and typically requires Board approval and, depending on what needs to change (authorized shares, charter/bylaws, new series), may trigger Preferred consent.
3. *Pay-to-play / recap mechanics* that shift dilution onto non-participating investors. This is exactly what pay-to-play is for, but it requires negotiating and documenting changes to Preferred economics and rights, which are protected by the consent items listed in the Restated Certificate.
If your board-level goal is “founders keep meaningful ownership without writing checks,” the usual board-discussable package is:
a small *founder option refresh* sized explicitly (example: 5–10% post-money pool allocated to founders/retention), and
• a *pay-to-play* feature where insiders who do not participate lose some combination of anti-dilution protection, pro rata, or Preferred status (conversion to common), subject to negotiation.
What to say in the board room, plainly
• A $2M pre priced round is mechanically feasible, but it is a down round vs Seed and triggers weighted-average anti-dilution in the charter.
• Any new series (unless explicitly junior) and most recap moves require Preferred approval.
• [PERSON_NAME_2000] already has a written right to buy up to 33% in the next Preferred financing, so “$250k match” needs to be explicitly reconciled with that right via side letter or waiver for this round.

content.content:
moved our jenkins jobs to my own machine tonight. the build boxes are HG's, they can go with the laptops whenever the sale needs them.

while I was in there I shut down the extra copy of CF's backend that was still running from the January redeploy, so CF's own account bills $62 a month now, just its live stacks. still on HG's AWS bill till March like Domino's.

**Games:** CF and DD come over through Sunset's sale. ZM stays with HG. DD made $183.11 in January, which covers the $140/mo its prod account bills now. ZM made $0.

**What the LLC runs, Mar–May:**
• DD prod account: $140/mo. Blake moves the billing by Mar 1.
• CF backend and auth: $62/mo after Blake killed the extra copy, not $95. Blake moves it by Mar 1.
• AppsFlyer free tier for CF: $0. You set it up by Mar 1.
• DD player support (support email): done, $0.
• Metabase $100, dbt $100, GitHub $48: Blake already pays these himself through May.

Everything else stays with HG: ZM's account, dev, the analytics pipeline, build machines, Figma, Slack/Google/Linear/Deel/Gusto/Intuit/Carta, the dev accounts, everything already cancelled, plus Calm Play since the LLC is the new one. The playable vendor is a one-off, so it isn't in the plan.

**Cost:** $450/mo total, so **$150/mo each**.
• You: $150 cash a month
• Me: $150 cash a month
• Blake: already pays $248, so he's $98 over his third. The LLC pays him back $98/mo out of our cash after the $202 of AWS.

Sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LgEZqiqfj4D8EBydE24LJu4WjxqRKuE558sTQDw6syQ/edit (shared with you and Blake)

content.text:
Your answer is ready for Monday: all 37 Linear issues have your call on them, the plan sheet is in your Drive and shared with Leonard and Blake, and the reply is posted in Leonard's DM thread. The LLC would cost $450 a month for March through May, which is $150 a month for each of you.

**The calls, following Leonard's ground rules:**
- **Games:** Combo Fighter comes over either way. Domino Delights also comes over, because it made $183.11 in January (from the warehouse's daily revenue table) and its hosting now bills $140 a month. Zombie Match made $0 in January, so it stays with HG. Both games come to the LLC through Sunset's sale.
- **What makes up the $450:**
  - Domino Delights' AWS hosting: $140
  - Combo Fighter's AWS backend: $62. Linear said $95, but Blake emailed on Feb 13 that he shut down an extra copy and it now bills $62.
  - Metabase $100, dbt $100 and GitHub $48: Blake already pays these on his own card through May.
- **Everything else stays with HG.** That includes Zombie Match's and the analytics AWS accounts, the build machines, Figma, Slack, Google, Linear, Deel, Gusto, Intuit, Carta, the Apple and Google Play accounts, and everything already cancelled in #winddown. The playable vendor ($3,750) is a one-off, so it's not in the monthly plan.
- **Calm Play LLC:** I marked it "not used". The ground rules say the LLC is a new one Leonard and Blake are setting up, which overrides Leonard's earlier comment that Calm Play could be it.

**Linear status:**
- **Todo (5):** Combo Fighter (you), Domino Delights (Leonard), Domino Delights' AWS hosting (Blake), Combo Fighter's AWS backend (Blake), and AppsFlyer (Leonard). The two games move when Sunset's sale closes; the other three by March 1.
- **Done (4):** Metabase, dbt, GitHub, and Domino Delights player support.
- **Canceled:** the other 28.

**How the money splits, using Leonard's email:**

| | Third | Already pays personally | Cash in per month |
|---|---|---|---|
| You | $150 | $0 | $150 |
| Leonard | $150 | $0 | $150 |
| Blake | $150 | $248 | −$98 |

Blake already pays more than his third, so the LLC pays him back $98 a month from your and Leonard's cash after covering the $202 of AWS.

The sheet uses the same columns as Leonard's Tuesday draft, with the shares table underneath. Leonard's draft had Figma going to the LLC; I didn't follow that, because HG prepaid it to Sep 11 and it just lapses then.

Sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LgEZqiqfj4D8EBydE24LJu4WjxqRKuE558sTQDw6syQ/edit
